basic_information.name: Make (formerly Integromat)
basic_information.creator: Originally founded as Integromat in Prague, Czech Republic. Acquired by Celonis (Munich-based process mining company) for over $100M in October 2020. Rebranded from Integromat to Make in 2022. Now operates as a subsidiary of Celonis with approximately 285 employees.
basic_information.description: Make is a visual workflow automation platform that enables users to design, build, and run complex multi-step automations across 2,500+ cloud applications and APIs without writing code. Its drag-and-drop scenario builder uses a node-and-connection canvas that makes data flow visible and intuitive, distinguishing it from simpler linear automation tools like Zapier. For entrepreneurs, Make offers a generous free tier (1,000 operations/month), native AI modules for OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, and Google Gemini, and a new AI Agents feature (launched April 2025) that lets workflows reason and adapt autonomously. As a Celonis subsidiary, Make benefits from enterprise credibility while maintaining accessible pricing for startups and small teams.
basic_information.release_date: 2012 (initial launch as Integromat). Rebranded as Make in 2022. Latest major release: Waves '25 event (April 2025) introducing Make AI Agents, Maia AI builder, and MCP Server.

technical_capabilities.underlying_models: Multi-provider via dedicated AI app modules: OpenAI (GPT-4o, GPT-4, O4 reasoning models), Anthropic (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus), Google (Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro), and 350+ AI application connectors including Grok, Hugging Face, Stability AI, and others. Users bring their own API keys for each provider. The HTTP module enables connection to any AI model with a REST API endpoint.
technical_capabilities.customization_depth: workflow-builder | code-extension. Make's primary interface is a visual scenario builder where users connect modules (triggers, actions, transformers) on a canvas. Advanced users can use the built-in JavaScript/JSON transformer modules, custom functions (Enterprise plan), and the HTTP/webhooks module to call arbitrary APIs. Custom apps can be built via the Make Developer Platform. Not a code-first environment but offers meaningful code-level extensibility.
technical_capabilities.api_access: Yes. Full REST API (Make API) for scenario management, execution triggering, and connection management. Available on Core plan and above. Webhook modules for inbound triggers. Any scenario can be exposed as an API endpoint via the Custom Webhook module.
technical_capabilities.deployment_options: Cloud-only. Make runs as a fully managed SaaS platform on AWS infrastructure. No self-hosting option. Enterprise customers run in a separately managed AWS environment isolated from self-service cloud. Scenarios can be triggered via webhooks, making integration with on-premise systems possible but the platform itself remains cloud-hosted.
technical_capabilities.ai_model_flexibility: multi-provider | bring-your-own-model (via API keys). Users choose between OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and 350+ AI apps. Different modules in the same scenario can use different AI providers. The HTTP module allows connecting to any model with a REST API. No vendor lock-in on AI model selection, though each provider requires its own API key configuration.

user_experience.target_user: business_user | marketer | enterprise_team. Make's visual builder is designed for non-developers who want more power than Zapier offers. Ideal for operations teams, marketers, and business analysts who need complex multi-step automations without coding. Also used by developers for rapid prototyping and integration work.
user_experience.learning_curve: hours. Basic scenarios achievable in 1-2 hours. The visual canvas is intuitive but more complex than Zapier's linear interface. Learning to use routers, iterators, and error handling takes a few days. Coming from Zapier, there is a learning curve adjustment due to the different paradigm (visual canvas vs. linear steps).
user_experience.setup_time: 15-30 minutes. No credit card required for free plan. First working scenario (e.g., Google Form to Google Sheets to email notification) achievable in 15-30 minutes using templates. AI-powered scenarios take 30-60 minutes due to API key setup.
user_experience.collaboration_features: Team workspaces with role-based access control (Teams and Enterprise plans). Scenario sharing and templates within organizations. Execution logs for audit trails. Enterprise adds SSO (SAML), auto-provisioning, audit logs, and advanced permission management. Free and Core plans are single-user.
user_experience.template_library: 1,000+ pre-built scenario templates covering CRM automation, marketing workflows, e-commerce, HR processes, AI workflows, and more. Templates are one-click importable and fully customizable. The Make community also contributes templates. Quality varies; some templates may be outdated. Additionally, over 7,000 community-shared templates are available through the broader ecosystem.
user_experience.visual_builder_type: drag-drop. Node-based visual scenario builder where users place modules on a 2D canvas and connect them with data flow lines. Supports branching (routers), loops (iterators), error handling paths, and parallel execution. The canvas model makes complex workflows more readable than linear builders. Maia (AI builder) adds natural-language scenario creation.

ai_and_rag_capabilities.rag_support: No native built-in RAG pipeline. Make does not include vector database nodes or document chunking modules natively. However, users can build RAG workflows by connecting external services: use an AI module to generate embeddings, store/query vectors via Pinecone or Weaviate HTTP integrations, and generate responses with OpenAI/Claude modules. The Make community has shared RAG-like patterns using combinations of Google Drive, text parsing, and LLM modules, but this requires manual orchestration rather than dedicated RAG nodes.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.agent_capabilities: multi-step | autonomous (via Make AI Agents). Launched at Waves '25 (April 2025), Make AI Agents are autonomous systems powered by LLMs that use reasoning to achieve goals within defined constraints. Agents are built directly on the scenario canvas in visual fashion. With 30,000+ available actions, agents can decide which tools and steps to execute. Users can observe agent reasoning in real time and intervene when needed. Features include 'Request Anything' for natural language processing within workflows and automatic sentiment analysis.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.model_selection: Multi-vendor. Users choose between OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and other AI providers within dedicated modules. Each AI module in a scenario can use a different provider. Model selection is configured per module via API keys. The platform updates to include the latest model versions (e.g., GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) as providers release them.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.prompt_management: Basic prompt configuration per AI module with system prompts, user prompts, and parameter controls (temperature, max tokens). Prompts can reference dynamic data from previous scenario steps using Make's variable mapping. No built-in prompt versioning, A/B testing, or optimization features. Prompt management is essentially manual within each module's configuration.

integration_and_ecosystem.key_integrations: Google Workspace (Sheets, Drive, Gmail, Calendar), Slack, Microsoft Teams, Notion, Airtable, HubSpot, Salesforce, Monday.com, Shopify, WooCommerce, Stripe, Mailchimp, Twilio, WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, AWS S3, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Stability AI, DeepL, Typeform, Webflow, WordPress, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Trello, Asana, Zendesk, Intercom, QuickBooks, NetSuite.
integration_and_ecosystem.integration_count: 2,500+ pre-built app connectors (some sources cite 1,800+ or 3,000+ depending on counting methodology). 400+ AI-specific integrations. The HTTP/webhooks module enables connection to any service with a REST API, extending reach beyond pre-built connectors. Over 40 new app connectors added at Waves '25.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_support: Yes. Make launched its own MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server, which turns Make scenarios into tools that external AI agents (Claude, GPT, Cursor, etc.) can call with precise inputs and outputs. The MCP Server runs via Streamable HTTP and Server-Sent Events (SSE). Users generate MCP tokens in their Make profile to control which scenarios are exposed. Make Academy offers a dedicated MCP course. Make also supports MCP Client functionality for AI agents within scenarios.
integration_and_ecosystem.webhook_support: Yes. Full webhook support both inbound (Custom Webhook module as scenario trigger, supporting GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) and outbound (HTTP module for callbacks). Webhooks support custom headers, authentication, and payload parsing. Instant triggers via webhooks are available on all plans.
integration_and_ecosystem.export_formats: Scenarios exportable as JSON blueprint files for backup and sharing. Data outputs depend on connected modules (spreadsheets, databases, files, APIs). No standalone app export; Make is a workflow engine. The Make API allows programmatic scenario management. Execution logs are viewable but not bulk-exportable on lower plans.

pricing_and_accessibility.pricing_model: freemium | usage-based. Free tier available with no credit card required. Paid plans are subscription-based with operation-based usage limits. Each action a module performs in a scenario counts as one operation. Data transfer is also metered. Pricing scales with operations consumed, scenarios active, and scheduling frequency.
pricing_and_accessibility.free_tier_limits: 1,000 operations/month, 2 active scenarios, 100 MB data transfer/month, 5 MB maximum file upload size, 15-minute minimum scheduling interval. Access to all 2,500+ integrations and the visual builder. No credit card required. Lifetime free plan (not a trial). Suitable for learning and small personal automations.
pricing_and_accessibility.paid_plans: Core: $10.59/month ($9/month annual) - 10,000 operations, unlimited active scenarios, 1-minute scheduling, Make API access, higher data transfer limits. Pro: $18.82/month ($16/month annual) - adds priority execution, full-text execution log search, custom variables. Teams: $34.12/month ($29/month annual) - adds team collaboration, role-based access, scenario templates, shared workspaces. Enterprise: custom pricing - adds SSO, auto-provisioning, audit logs, 24/7 support, technical account manager, SLAs, custom functions, dynamic connections, larger file sizes, overage protection.
pricing_and_accessibility.open_source: no (proprietary). Make is a closed-source, proprietary SaaS platform. No source code is publicly available. No self-hosting option.
pricing_and_accessibility.self_hosting_option: Not available. Make is exclusively a cloud-hosted SaaS platform. Enterprise customers receive an isolated AWS environment but cannot run Make on their own infrastructure. This is a key differentiator versus n8n (self-hostable) and a limitation for organizations requiring full on-premise deployment.
pricing_and_accessibility.data_residency_and_sovereignty: Cloud-hosted on AWS. Make is GDPR compliant with a published Data Processing Agreement (DPA) including Standard Contractual Clauses. SOC 2 Type II certified. ISO 27001 certified. CCPA compliant. Enterprise customers run in isolated AWS environments. Being a Czech company (now Celonis subsidiary, Munich-headquartered), Make has EU roots and EU-based operations. However, specific data center region selection (e.g., EU-only hosting) details are not publicly documented for non-Enterprise plans. Encrypted OAuth connections used for all integrations.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the visual workflow automation category, positioned between Zapier (simpler, more integrations, more expensive) and n8n (more technical, self-hostable, open-core). Make is widely recognized as offering the best balance of visual power, affordability, and flexibility among cloud-only automation platforms. Particularly strong for complex multi-step workflows where Zapier's linear model becomes limiting. The Celonis acquisition provides enterprise credibility and process mining synergies.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Disney, ServiceNow, and Madison Square Garden (via GAP Consulting). FranklinCovey (replaced $60K legacy system, reduced HR workflows from 30 days to 2 hours). ChargeGuru (reduced lead import time from 1 week to 15 minutes). HIA (50+ automated processes for athlete onboarding, finance, and communications). Celonis itself uses Make internally (reduced AI processing costs by 99.7%). Lightpost (content marketing automation at scale).
adoption_and_market.community_size: 250,000+ customers as of 2020 (likely significantly higher by 2025-2026). 200,000+ learners on Make Academy. Active community forum at community.make.com. 1,000+ official templates plus 7,000+ community-shared templates. 285 employees. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Integromat was bootstrapped (raised $0 in external funding before acquisition). Acquired by Celonis for over $100M in October 2020. Celonis itself is valued at approximately $13B (as of 2022 Series D) with $771M ARR in 2023 and has raised over $1.4B total. Make operates as a subsidiary; separate valuation and revenue figures for Make are not publicly disclosed. Celonis debuted at No. 3 on the 2025 Fortune Future 50 list. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: Zapier (8,000+ integrations, simplest UX, per-task pricing, most expensive at scale, no self-hosting), n8n (400+ core nodes, self-hostable, open-core, execution-based pricing, strongest AI/LangChain integration, steeper learning curve), Activepieces (open-source, simpler), Power Automate (Microsoft ecosystem, enterprise-focused). Key Make differentiators: best-in-class visual canvas builder (2D node graph vs. linear steps), strong price-to-power ratio (more affordable than Zapier for complex workflows), native AI Agents with visual reasoning, MCP Server for AI interoperability, Maia natural-language builder, and Celonis enterprise backing.
adoption_and_market.ecosystem_lock_in_risk: medium. Scenarios are exportable as JSON blueprints, but the format is proprietary and not directly portable to competitors. No self-hosting means dependency on Make's cloud infrastructure and pricing decisions. Integrations use standard APIs, so switching to another automation platform is feasible but requires rebuilding workflows. The free tier and affordable pricing reduce financial lock-in risk. Data passes through Make's servers during execution.

teaching_and_classroom.class_project_idea:
Project 1: 'AI-Powered Customer Feedback Analyzer' (45 min) - Students create a Make scenario that: (a) watches a Google Form for new customer feedback submissions, (b) sends the feedback text to OpenAI/Claude via an AI module for sentiment analysis and category classification, (c) routes positive feedback to a 'Testimonials' Google Sheet and negative feedback to a 'Issues' sheet with suggested response drafts, (d) sends a Slack/email notification for urgent negative feedback. This teaches: visual automation design, AI integration in business processes, conditional routing, and real-time alerting. Deliverable: working scenario + 2-minute pitch on how this could save a startup 5-10 hours/week in customer support triage.

Project 2: 'Lead-to-Meeting Automation Pipeline' (60 min) - Students build a multi-step scenario that: (a) triggers on new HubSpot/Airtable contact creation, (b) uses an AI module to enrich the lead by generating a company summary from the website URL, (c) scores the lead based on configurable criteria, (d) for high-score leads, automatically drafts a personalized outreach email using Claude/GPT and sends it via Gmail, (e) creates a follow-up task in Notion/Trello. This demonstrates: CRM automation, AI-powered personalization, lead scoring logic, and the power of no-code to replace manual sales processes. Deliverable: working pipeline + unit economics calculation (cost per lead processed vs. manual processing).

teaching_and_classroom.student_prerequisites: nothing | basic prompting. Make's visual builder requires no coding knowledge. Students should understand basic automation concepts (trigger-action logic) which can be explained in 5 minutes. For AI module projects, basic understanding of what LLMs are and how prompts work is helpful but not required. API key setup (OpenAI/Claude) can be walked through in class.
teaching_and_classroom.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools) - primary fit for hands-on workflow building with AI modules, demonstrates how prompt engineering applies in automated workflows. Session 3 (Framing & Managing AI Projects) - useful for Build vs Buy discussions (Make vs. n8n vs. custom code), illustrates CRISP-DM deployment phase. Session 4 (AI Business Models) - illustrative for unit economics analysis (cost per operation vs. manual labor cost).

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Make is ideal for non-technical founders and small business teams (pre-seed to Series A) who need powerful automation without hiring developers. Best use cases: (1) Operations automation (CRM sync, lead routing, invoice processing, customer onboarding workflows) starting from the free tier; (2) AI-enhanced business processes (sentiment analysis, content generation, email personalization) using native AI modules with pay-as-you-go API keys; (3) Rapid prototyping of workflow-heavy MVPs where the product involves connecting multiple services (e.g., marketplace, booking platform, content pipeline). Particularly strong for marketing teams, agencies, and solopreneurs who need Zapier-level ease with more complex routing capabilities. Less suitable for teams needing self-hosting, data sovereignty, or heavy custom code integration; those teams should consider n8n instead.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_mvp: Hours to days. A basic automation scenario (e.g., form to CRM to notification) takes 15-30 minutes using templates. An AI-powered workflow (e.g., feedback analysis pipeline, lead scoring) takes 1-2 hours. A full operational backend with 5-10 interconnected scenarios takes 1-3 days. Make's visual builder and template library significantly accelerate development compared to custom coding. The free tier supports real development, not just demos.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Make when: your team is non-technical or lightly technical, you need complex visual workflows with branching logic, you want quick setup with no infrastructure management, you need 2,500+ pre-built integrations, and your data processing volume stays within plan limits. Use n8n when: you need self-hosting for data sovereignty, your team is technical, you want execution-based pricing for high-volume workflows, or you need deep AI/LangChain integration. Use Zapier when: you want the absolute simplest setup, need the widest integration library (8,000+), or only need simple linear automations. Build custom when: you need sub-second latency, handle millions of events daily, or require deep integration with proprietary systems. Cost comparison: a 10-step workflow running 10,000 times/month costs ~$10.59/month on Make Core (10,000 ops) vs. $250+ on Zapier vs. ~$30/month self-hosted n8n (unlimited).
key_lessons: 1. The visual canvas is Make's superpower: Unlike Zapier's linear steps, Make's 2D canvas with routers, iterators, and error handling paths makes complex workflows readable and maintainable. This visual clarity is crucial when automations grow beyond simple triggers; invest time learning the canvas paradigm rather than forcing linear thinking.

2. Operations math matters for cost control: Every module execution counts as one operation. A scenario with 5 modules running 200 times/month consumes 1,000 operations (your entire free tier). Before building, map out your expected operation count: multiply modules per scenario by expected monthly executions. Use filters early in scenarios to prevent unnecessary downstream operations.

3. AI modules unlock disproportionate value at low cost: Adding a single OpenAI or Claude module to an existing automation (e.g., sentiment analysis on support tickets, content summarization for newsletters) can transform a basic workflow into an intelligent one. The AI API cost per call ($0.001-0.01) is negligible compared to the business value of automated intelligence.

4. Start with templates, then customize: Make's 1,000+ templates provide battle-tested starting points. Import a template for your use case, run it once to understand the data flow, then customize. This is 3-5x faster than building from scratch and avoids common architectural mistakes.

5. Plan your migration path: Make's proprietary cloud model means switching costs increase as you build more scenarios. Document your automations externally, keep API integrations standard (avoid Make-specific features when generic HTTP calls work), and periodically evaluate whether the cost-benefit ratio still holds as your usage scales.

confidence.data_quality: High. Information sourced from Make's official website, Help Center, Academy, blog posts (including Waves '25 announcements), Celonis financial data via GetLatka and Contrary Research, independent reviews from Hackceleration, Digital Project Manager, Lindy, and Relay.app, comparison analyses from Digidop and Contabo, and Make's official security and GDPR documentation.
confidence.cross_reference: Pricing confirmed across Make's official pricing page, The Digital Project Manager, Lindy, Relay.app, and ThinkPeak AI. Integration count (2,500+) confirmed via multiple independent reviews. Celonis acquisition ($100M+) confirmed via Crunchbase, Celonis Wikipedia, and MakeItFuture. GDPR/SOC2 compliance confirmed via Make's official security page and community forums. Free tier (1,000 ops/month) confirmed across 5+ independent sources. AI Agents launch (April 2025) confirmed via official Make blog and TechInformed.
confidence.caveats: Integration count varies by source (1,500+ to 3,000+) depending on counting methodology and date; 2,500+ is the most commonly cited figure. Make.com-specific revenue and user count data is not publicly disclosed separately from Celonis; the 250,000 customer figure is from 2020 (pre-acquisition era). Pricing may have changed since data collection; Make announced plan adjustments in 2025. The AI Agents feature was initially in closed beta; general availability status should be verified. Make's lack of self-hosting is a significant limitation for data sovereignty use cases compared to n8n. Operation-based pricing can become expensive for high-volume, multi-step scenarios.
